court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: Indian country status
issues.why: Federal jurisdiction under MCA/GCA/ACA depends on whether the conduct occurred in Indian country.

issues.label: Defendant Indian status
issues.why: MCA applies to Indians and GCA/ACA applicability depends on each defendant’s Indian/non-Indian status.

issues.label: Victim Indian status
issues.why: GCA exceptions and federal/state jurisdictional rules turn on whether the victim is Indian.

issues.label: MCA predicate offense
issues.why: Court must confirm Oklahoma child abuse/neglect qualify as MCA-enumerated offenses (or fit within a listed category) for Mr. Smith.

issues.label: MCA incorporates state law
issues.why: If MCA applies, court must identify how Oklahoma elements and penalties are incorporated for the federal offense.

issues.label: GCA applicability to Mrs. Smith
issues.why: Court must determine whether §1152 applies to a non-Indian defendant with an Indian victim in Indian country.

issues.label: ACA assimilation prerequisites
issues.why: ACA applies only if no federal statute punishes the same conduct, requiring a “gap” analysis.

issues.label: ACA in Indian country
issues.why: Court must assess proper use of ACA via GCA for crimes in Indian country involving non-Indian defendants.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm district court had statutory and constitutional authority to adjudicate each count.

issues.label: Castro-Huerta effect
issues.why: Court must decide whether Castro-Huerta alters federal jurisdiction over non-Indian-on-Indian crimes or merely confirms concurrent state power.

issues.label: Concurrent state jurisdiction
issues.why: Even if state has jurisdiction, court must decide whether that affects federal prosecution or creates preemption/dual-sovereignty issues.

issues.label: Double jeopardy concerns
issues.why: Court must consider whether any state proceedings occurred and whether dual sovereignty or collateral estoppel is implicated.

issues.label: Indictment sufficiency
issues.why: Court must ensure the superseding indictment alleged all essential elements, jurisdictional facts, and aiding-and-abetting theory.

issues.label: Variance/identity confusion
issues.why: Victim identified as H.M./M.V./K.B. raises potential variance or prejudice affecting notice and verdict integrity.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting authority
issues.why: Court must decide whether 18 U.S.C. §2 permits aiding/abetting liability when the principal charge is under MCA or ACA/GCA.

issues.label: Non-Indian aiding MCA
issues.why: Court must resolve whether a non-Indian can be convicted as an aider/abettor of an MCA offense charged against an Indian principal.

issues.label: Indian aiding GCA/ACA
issues.why: Court must resolve whether an Indian can be convicted as an aider/abettor of a GCA/ACA offense where §1152 would not apply to an Indian principal.

issues.label: Proper principal identification
issues.why: Aiding-and-abetting requires proof someone committed the underlying offense; court must ensure jury could find a qualifying principal offense.

issues.label: Instruction correctness
issues.why: Court must determine whether the aiding-and-abetting instruction accurately stated law and elements for each defendant and count.

issues.label: Instruction preservation
issues.why: Court must decide whether defendants properly preserved the instruction/jurisdiction objections and the resulting standard of review.

issues.label: Harmless or plain error
issues.why: If any instructional error occurred, court must apply the correct appellate prejudice/harmless-error framework.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence
issues.why: Rule 29 issues require determining whether evidence was sufficient for each element of child abuse, neglect, and aiding/abetting.

issues.label: Oklahoma elements interpretation
issues.why: Court must interpret §843.5(A) and (C) elements, mental states, and definitions as incorporated into federal charges.

issues.label: Unanimity requirements
issues.why: Court must consider whether jury needed unanimity on specific acts (abuse vs neglect episodes) or theories supporting each count.

issues.label: Duplicity/unit of prosecution
issues.why: Court must ensure each count charged a single offense and clarify unit of prosecution for ongoing abuse/neglect.

issues.label: Joinder and severance
issues.why: Joint trial of spouses and cross-aiding theories may raise Rule 8/14 concerns about prejudice and need for severance.

issues.label: Confrontation/Bruton issues
issues.why: Court must consider whether any statements by one spouse were introduced against the other in a way violating confrontation rights.

issues.label: Evidentiary fairness
issues.why: Court must assess admission of abuse/neglect evidence, medical proof, and any Rule 403/404(b) issues affecting verdict integrity.

issues.label: Sentencing guideline selection
issues.why: For Mr. Smith, court must determine the correct guideline under §1B1.2 and §2X5.1 (most analogous guideline) or justify none.

issues.label: Analogous guideline analysis
issues.why: Court must compare §843.5(A) conduct to potentially analogous guidelines (e.g., aggravated assault, assault, child-related guidelines) and explain choice.

issues.label: Procedural reasonableness
issues.why: Court must decide whether guidelines miscalculation occurred and whether sentencing explanation satisfied procedural requirements.

issues.label: Statutory maximums
issues.why: Court must determine the correct statutory maximum/minimum penalties for assimilated/state-law offenses as applied federally.

issues.label: Consecutive/concurrent authority
issues.why: Court must confirm legal basis for concurrent sentences and whether grouping or multiple-count rules affect the advisory calculation.

issues.label: Guidelines anchoring error
issues.why: If court treated range as “up to life” without proper guideline, it may have improperly anchored the §3553(a) analysis.

issues.label: Substantive reasonableness
issues.why: Court must assess whether 180/240-month sentences are substantively reasonable under §3553(a) given facts and comparators.

issues.label: Victim-impact letter timeliness
issues.why: Court must decide whether late-submitted letters violated Rule 32, due process, or required continuance for meaningful rebuttal.

issues.label: Who is a CVRA victim
issues.why: Court must determine whether letter writers qualify as “crime victims” under 18 U.S.C. §3771(e)(2).

issues.label: Consideration of non-victims
issues.why: Even if not CVRA victims, court must decide whether sentencing court may consider such letters and under what limits.

issues.label: Notice and opportunity to respond
issues.why: Court must ensure defendants had a fair opportunity to contest factual assertions in letters before sentencing.

issues.label: Reliability of sentencing info
issues.why: Due process requires sentencing facts have sufficient indicia of reliability, including claims in victim-impact submissions.

issues.label: Rule 29 timing (second motion)
issues.why: Court must determine whether Mrs. Smith’s post-sentencing amended Rule 29 motion was filed within the strict deadline or permitted extension.

issues.label: Rule 33 timing (second motion)
issues.why: Court must decide whether new-trial motion met Rule 33 deadlines and whether “newly discovered evidence” exception applies.

issues.label: Authority to extend deadlines
issues.why: Court must address whether Rule 45 permits extending Rule 29/33 deadlines and whether district court had jurisdiction to entertain late motions.

issues.label: Characterization of filing
issues.why: Court must determine whether the “amended second motion” relates back to a timely motion or is a new untimely motion.

issues.label: Standard for new trial
issues.why: If timely, court must apply Rule 33 standards (interest of justice or newly discovered evidence) to asserted grounds.

issues.label: Remedy on guideline error
issues.why: If guideline error found, court must decide appropriate remedy (vacate sentence, remand for resentencing) and scope of remand.

issues.label: Remedy on instruction error
issues.why: If aiding/abetting instruction invalid, court must decide whether reversal, acquittal, or new trial is required for each count/defendant.

issues.label: Effect on both defendants
issues.why: Court must consider whether an error affecting aiding/abetting or jurisdiction as to one defendant impacts the other’s convictions.

issues.label: Preservation of jurisdiction claim
issues.why: Court must decide whether Castro-Huerta jurisdiction argument was timely raised and whether jurisdictional challenges can be forfeited.

issues.label: Article III case/controversy
issues.why: Court must ensure appellate issues are live, not moot, and that requested relief is within the court’s power.
